title: Task context
description: One repository's task context file (<work>/tasks-<slug>.context.json), handed to its task decomposer as `task context` beside the repository's spec context (`repository context`, spec-context.schema.json), whose `items` are what the Story builds. The step `task_decomposition.context` (orchestrator/flows/task_decomposition.py) writes it and validates it against this file. It holds facts and pointers only; the commands named below print what the matrix and the bead tracker hold.

stacks.description: Each stack the Story builds in, with the matrix ids of the entries it builds there. For these stacks and the upstream stacks in dependsOn, `atw-matrix work --id <stack> --not-epic <epic>` names real candidate Tasks of other Epics. Same-stack work can overlap; an upstream candidate is a prerequisite only when the Task consumes its output. The shared capabilities a Task must use are derived from the items it cites, not stated by the decomposer.

existingTasks.description: The Task beads under the Story that are started, or that elaboration did not write: each is reused, not rewritten. `bd show <id>` prints a Task's description.

elabKey.description: The Task's elaboration key, or null when elaboration did not write it.

requirementIds.description: The ids of the items and requirements the Task cites.

dependsOn.description: What the Tasks depend on outside what the Story builds, including dependencies of the stacks holding that work: context, never work assigned to this Story. The decomposer uses named upstream stacks to discover real external producer Tasks.

producerCandidates.description: Current real Tasks in the supplied own and upstream stacks, including closed Tasks and their parent Story status and recorded publication and deployment verification. Candidates are evidence, never automatic blockers. Closed alone does not establish deployed readiness.
